title: Misty Western Ghats Valley
project: TODO: client, film, album or game this cue belongs to
brief: TODO: the words the client actually used, verbatim
audience: TODO: who hears it, where they hear it, and what they already know
purpose: a continuous 90-second slow orchestral adagio over the misty green valleys of the Western Ghats at dawn
point_of_view: narrator, not a character: the camera floats, it does not walk, so no pulse and no urgent register
job: set the place before the first word of voice-over
hold one unbroken mood: no key change, no drum
leave the middle of the spectrum free for the narration
end on the note it began, so the cut out is not a shock
story: Mist, then a ridge, then the sun breaking over it, then the descent: one long breath with a single crest at 52 s.

sections.name: open on the valley
sections.action: slow aerial push through moving mist, no editing
sections.music: one held flute note over string harmonics; nothing else enters

sections.name: the ridge appears
sections.action: the ridge resolves out of the mist
sections.music: the flute phrase answers itself a fifth lower; celli enter under it

sections.name: crest
sections.action: the camera clears the ridge; the valley floor opens
sections.music: the low celli move to the tonic; strings widen; the dynamic crest lands at 52 s

sections.name: sun
sections.music: the widest string spread of the cue; the flute holds one long note, then rests

sections.name: descent
sections.action: the camera drops toward the canopy
sections.music: the opening figure inverted, celli only, the mist bed returns

sections.name: final frame
sections.music: solo flute on the tonic, one breath, then the room tail

motifs.name: dawn call
motifs.shape: three rising notes, bare fifth, no vibrato
motifs.returns: answered a fifth lower at 18 s, inverted at 70 s, alone on the tonic at 86 s

hits.why: a movement inside the shot, not an edit: a soft sync, so a few frames either way do not matter

hits.sound: cello low C under the strings
hits.why: hard cut to the valley floor; a hard sync point, on the frame
the cue's own crest, one beat after the cut so the cut lands first

must_hear: nothing masking 250-3800 Hz while the narration speaks

references: in words, not a track: a solo flute over slow celli, the colour of a nature documentary opening, no percussion
the crest behaves like a held breath released, not like a trailer hit
